summary: Wolfgang Franke was a sinologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Hamburg. He held posts at Sichuan University and Peking University before serving as chair of sinology at the University of Hamburg from circa 1950 to 1977.

Wolfgang Morgenroth was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD under Richard Hauschild at the University of Jena and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He held posts at Jena, Greifswald, and Humboldt University of Berlin, later visiting Pune and Potsdam.

Wolfgang Schultz was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He worked at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and was appointed Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

Wolfgang Voigt was a scholar in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He founded the Verzeichnis der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland and served as its General Editor from circa 1957 to 1982.

Wolfram Eberhard worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied under Ferdinand Lessing at Humboldt University and the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen. He taught in China, curated at the Grassi Museum, was professor at Ankara University, and later sociology professor at UC Berkeley.
Woncheol Yun is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Stony Brook University. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University, attested in 2012.

Woosung Huh is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He was attested in 2012 as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University.
Wouter J. Hanegraaff is a religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University from circa 1982 to 1995. He held a post at the University of Amsterdam circa 1999.
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1999, he studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche.
Xi Cao is a scholar in computational fields and Tibetology. Xi Cao has held posts at Minzu University of China and Tibet University.
Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong by 2016, with doctoral supervision under K. L. Dhammajoti in 1995.

Xianlin Ji was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. After studying at Tsinghua, he completed his PhD at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg. He held prominent roles at Peking University, CASS, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Xiaoling Wu was a sinologist and Indologist who held posts at Peking University, Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and served as a professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoming Hou is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. Hou was a doctoral student at Ghent University and served as a postdoctoral researcher there, both attested in 2026.
Xiaoting Wei is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng Mei Ku, attested in 2004.

Xinchuan Huang was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher who studied at Peking University (~1953–1958). He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from circa 1978 to 1998, with his affiliation attested through 2007.

Xinru Liu is a historian and Indologist who earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. Liu served as a professor at CASS's Institute of World History and became Professor Emeritus at The College of New Jersey.
Xiuzhi Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a master's degree at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen, attested in 2006.

Xu Dishan was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Yenching, Columbia, and Oxford. He held academic posts at Peking University (~1926–1935), Tsinghua University (~1927–1935), and the University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).

Xue Yu is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Posts include assistant professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010), Visiting Professor of Buddhism at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), and professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
